article_title: .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14 Ship Out-of-Band Fixes for a Brotli Buffer Overflow, CVE-2026-111497, Alongside .NET 11 Release Candidate 3

content_preview.title: .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14 Ship Out-of-Band Fixes for a Brotli Buffer Overflow, CVE-2026-111497, Alongside .NET 11 Release Candidate 3
content_preview.summary: Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release fixes CVE-2026-111497 in Brotli decompression and a Linux tarball ownership flaw, and re-releases two advisories the October 13 release did not fully address.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Microsoft has released out-of-band (OOB) security updates for .NET 8, .NET 9 and .NET 10, along with .NET 11 Release Candidate 3, according to the [.NET Blog post of October 25, 2026](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/dotnet-october-2026-oob-security-updates/). The post says: "We recommend updating as soon as possible." The fixes for the supported lines ship as .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14; .NET 11 is covered by its third release candidate, a pre-release build.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Briefing (595 words, range 300-800). Title is 139 characters (cap 150). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure; neutral tone; no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: Snapshots source-0..3.html.gz read from disk (text-extracted, scripts stripped) and re-fetched live with curl (HTTP 200 for all three devblogs pages) with identical key text. source-0 (OOB post, dated October 25th, 2026, author Rahul Bhandari): confirms 'out-of-band (OOB) security updates for .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10, along with .NET 11 Release Candidate 3'; 'We recommend updating as soon as possible.'; CVE-2026-111497 description verbatim ('A buffer overflow vulnerability exists in .NET's use of the Brotli decompression algorithm. This vulnerability may allow an unauthenticated attacker to read or corrupt process memory. This could lead to information disclosure, denial of service, or elevation of privilege.', affected platforms 'All Platforms'); CVE-2026-114148 ('Unsafe ownership metadata in affected .NET tarballs could allow a local attacker to modify files and gain elevated privileges', Linux; .NET 10/11 source-build tarballs only; .NET 8/9 also ASP.NET Core tarball distributions 'including users who do not build .NET from source'); affected-application list (ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic response decompression, System.IO.Compression Brotli APIs), 'not enabled by default', '.NET Framework is not affected'; re-released CVE-2026-70197 (SocketAsyncEventArgs memory corruption; .NET 8, 9, 10, 11) and CVE-2026-102870 (Blazor WebAssembly debugger; .NET 10 and 11) 'because the October 13, 2026 release did not fully address these issues. Today's updates provide those fixes.'; version table 8.0.33 / 9.0.22 / 10.0.14 / 11 RC3; '.NET 11 RC2 users should update to RC3 to receive these fixes.'; deployment guidance. No severity or CVSS score is given in the post, and the article states none. The post's table is the only place the versions are tied to the fixes (the table accompanies the security section); the article's claim that these are the fixed versions is a fair reading. source-1 (servicing post): 'refreshed with the latest update as of October 13, 2026'; release versions 10.0.13 / 9.0.21 / 8.0.32 confirmed. source-2 (RC2 post, October 13, 2026): 'comes with a go-live support license' confirmed; the article cites it only for that and does not attribute RC3 contents to it. RC3 availability is attributed to the OOB post only. source-3 (Node.js advisory): 'Node.js Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write permits remote code execution (CVE-2026-111497) - (high)' and 'A flaw in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js ...' confirmed verbatim; same identifier. Allowlist: devblogs.microsoft.com (line 853) and nodejs.org (line 1137) present by exact hostname. Microsoft/.NET Foundation first-party; Node.js advisory is a different project's first-party page. manifest suspicious_patterns null for all four sources. MSRC page returned 200 but is script-rendered. Corroboration only (not cited): the MITRE CVE record for CVE-2026-111497 (assigner Google) describes an out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c), versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0, and links the Node.js advisory; this is consistent with the article's careful claim of a shared identifier only. CVE-2026-114148 and CVE-2026-70197 are Microsoft-assigned records.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, version, CVE id, date and quote traces to the cited sources. Quotes verified verbatim: 'We recommend updating as soon as possible.', 'may allow an unauthenticated attacker to read or corrupt process memory', 'could allow a local attacker to modify files and gain elevated privileges', 'including users who do not build .NET from source', 'because the October 13, 2026 release did not fully address these issues', '.NET 11 RC2 users should update to RC3 to receive these fixes.' Overlap with Node.js: article claims only a shared CVE identifier, says the .NET post does not name the root cause or relate the fixes, and does not claim 'same bug' or 'upstream library'. The .NET post indeed contains no such statement. Internal link /article/2026-10/22-nodejs-security-releases-26121-24221-and-22234-fix-ten-cves-four-rated-high-including-a-brotli-decoder-out-of-bounds-write resolves to an existing article and is described accurately. 'What We Don't Know' items (no severity/CVSS, no exploitation statement, no reporter, no explanation for incomplete October 13 fix) are consistent with the post text. Minor: 'two new CVEs' is the writer's gloss on the post's two listed CVEs; acceptable.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; the only editorial-style content is the explicit limitation of what the sources do not say.
editor_notes.originality: New story. The related Herald Node.js security-release article (2026-10/22) covers a different project's release; this article cites it for context, adds the .NET-specific facts and does not duplicate it. No earlier Herald coverage of this .NET OOB release found.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully scoped first-party security-release Briefing; claims stay within the sources, with disciplined handling of the shared CVE identifier. Approve. Featured candidacy: 2 - out-of-band security release for a widely used platform with an unauthenticated memory-corruption fix, fully verified against first-party posts
